label: Topshelf Records
description: Ratboys' debut LP, cut soon after Julia Steiner and Dave Sagan relocated from Indiana to Chicago: unhurried, twang-flecked indie rock built around Steiner's plainspoken voice and long, patient song structures. A quieter, more folk-adjacent record than the band's later output, closer to their alt-country roots.
lineage: Grew out of Steiner and Sagan's college-band beginnings at Notre Dame; set the twangy-indie template the band expanded on GN and Printer's Devil.

label: Topshelf Records
description: Second Ratboys LP, named Rolling Stone's under-the-radar pick of 2017: warm, unhurried indie rock with country phrasing and Steiner's conversational storytelling. Quieter and more spacious than the band's later, harder-rocking records.
lineage: Bridges the band's early alt-country leanings with the bigger, distorted guitar sound they'd bring on Printer's Devil.

label: Topshelf Records
description: Ratboys' loudest, most confident record to that point: bigger choruses and full-band muscle layered over the same plainspoken, twang-inflected songwriting. Widely reviewed as the band's breakthrough.
lineage: Marks the move from their earlier folk-adjacent sound toward the anthemic guitar rock of The Window and Singin' to an Empty Chair.

label: Topshelf Records
description: A tenth-anniversary record built from older songs and new ones, capturing the full band (with the 'Go Outside' single) at their most direct and hooky. Sits between the loose twang of GN and the polish of The Window.
lineage: A victory-lap record marking Ratboys' first decade before their Chris Walla-produced pivot.

label: Topshelf Records
description: Chris Walla-produced fifth LP blending alt-rock, country twang and a little emo, widely called the culmination of Ratboys' patient songwriting. Highlights include the elegiac 'Black Earth, WI' and the wired 'Morning Zoo'.
lineage: Josh Terry calls it the culmination of 15 years of Ratboys' inviting songwriting; sits alongside Wednesday and MJ Lenderman in the current wave of twangy Midwest/Southern indie rock.

label: New West Records
description: Ratboys' sixth LP: massive-sounding, anthemic indie rock with lilting twang and frantic shredding, released February 2026 on New West. Terry called it a model of how indie rock should sound.
lineage: Continues the arc from AOID's quiet twang through The Window's alt-rock/country/emo blend.

label: 12XU
description: Florry's turn toward Gram Parsons-style Cosmic American Music: pedal steel, honky-tonk piano and Neil Young-indebted guitar wrapped around Francie Medosch's newly hopeful songwriting after a run of darker material.
lineage: Draws directly on Parsons' Cosmic American Music and Neil Young; set up the caustic barroom twang of The Holey Bible.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A four-song, ramshackle punk-country EP built for beers in a small booze-stained room, as Josh Terry described it; a loose bridge between Big Fall and the fuller-band Holey Bible.
lineage: Part of the same Dear Life Records-era run of scrappy, caustic Philly country as The Holey Bible.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Florry's Dear Life Records debut proper: raucous, barroom-ready country-rock with a half-broken pedal steel, fiddle and a full band behind Francie Medosch's caustic, warble-voiced songwriting. Terry called it ice-cold-beer music between the Replacements and Drive-By Truckers.
lineage: Cemented Florry's place in the Dear Life/Sophomore Lounge-adjacent indie-twang scene alongside Greg Freeman and Lily Seabird.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Florry's sophomore full-band album, cut with Colin Miller at Drop of Sun: rambunctious barroom twang with Dylan/Rolling Thunder energy alongside quieter, more understated songs. Recorded after Medosch's move from Philly to Burlington.
lineage: Produced by Colin Miller, the Asheville figure behind records by MJ Lenderman, Wednesday and Merce Lemon, tying Florry into that Asheville-Burlington indie-twang network.

label: Loose Music
description: Debut LP from Norwich's Brown Horse: stark, road-worn alt-country recorded live over four days, praised by Uncut and Mojo. Establishes the band's twangy, weary songwriting before the fuller sound of All the Right Weaknesses.
lineage: A UK band working directly in the American alt-country/Crazy Horse tradition, later drawing comparisons to Wednesday and Greg Freeman.

label: Loose Music
description: Brown Horse's second LP, tracked live in a week at Sickroom Studios: soaring guitars, blissful pedal steel and earnest vocals melding slacker-rock, folk and alt-country. Terry placed it near Greg Freeman, Wednesday and Neil Young.
lineage: Cites Lucinda Williams, Jason Molina, the Breeders and Silver Jews as touchstones; part of the UK's small but active indie-twang scene.

label: Fluff and Gravy Records
description: Brown Horse's third LP: brooding, twangy guitar rock with fuzzy riffs, pedal steel and country-rock arrangements, released April 2026 on Fluff and Gravy.
lineage: Continues the band's Norfolk-recorded alt-country arc from Reservoir and All the Right Weaknesses.

note: Debut LP mentioned in Florry's Big Fall Bandcamp bio (Sister Polygon, 2018); no tracklist or dedicated page found to confirm key tracks.

label: Big Legal Mess Records
description: Tampa-born, New Orleans-based Dollbaum's debut LP: pandemic-recorded, dark rural storytelling in a rangy baritone, compared to Richard Buckner and Arthur Russell for its lyricism drawn from Harry Crews and Denis Johnson-style Southern gothic detail.
lineage: Establishes Dollbaum in the same alt-country storytelling lineage as Townes Van Zandt and Jason Molina, later cited explicitly on Birds of Paradise.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Six-song EP reflecting on a friend's death via drives through Florida backroads; hushed, tragic story-songs tracked with Clay Jones, a brief bridge between Wellswood and Birds of Paradise.
lineage: Continues Dollbaum's alt-country storytelling into the Dear Life Records fold alongside Florry and Greg Freeman.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Dollbaum's second LP: roaring Americana shading into tender folk, sung in a rangy, raspy baritone with strong harmonies; a goodbye letter to lost loved ones set in Florida's pine flatwoods.
lineage: Explicitly follows Townes Van Zandt and Jason Molina while stepping out of their shadow, per the album's own liner note.

label: Self-released
description: Early self-released Spencer Radcliffe LP: sparse, home-recorded songs that anticipate the twangier, more rock-oriented turn of his later solo work.
lineage: An early entry in Radcliffe's long solo catalogue that eventually feeds into the twangier Ohio Vision.
borderline_note: Sound not directly confirmed as twang/country; included as completion of an artist mapped to C1, sequenced before his rockier records.

label: Run For Cover Records
description: Radcliffe's debut full-length proper, recorded alone in a converted Chicago lighthouse studio: patchwork indie pop and lo-fi textures held together by his flat, equivocal voice.
lineage: Follows the Brown Horse split tape on Orchid Tapes; part of the same Run for Cover/Topshelf-adjacent 2010s indie underground as Ratboys.

label: Orindal Records
description: Radcliffe's first fully solo record in a decade: fuzzy, hypnotic rock and 'hayseed jammers' chronicling six years of returning home to Ohio, mixed by Bradford Krieger. Twangy Midwest indie rock, propulsive and relaxed by turns.
lineage: Follows two full-band records as Spencer Radcliffe & Everyone Else; feeds directly into the current wave of Midwest indie-twang alongside Ratboys and i26connector.

label: Self-released
description: Asheville project's seven-song debut, self-tagged 'Emo Southern Rock': wailing pedal steel and booming riffs under conversational lyrics swinging from barroom talk to apocalyptic brooding.
lineage: Part of the Asheville scene around MJ Lenderman and Wednesday (fans of both on Bandcamp), blending twangy Southern rock with an emo-adjacent intensity.
borderline_note: Self-tagged 'Emo Southern Rock'; could also fit C9 (twangy emo crossover) as secondary.

label: Self-released
description: 21-year-old Zane Mclaughlin's studio debut as Oldstar: raucous, meaty overdriven country rock with fiddle and outlaw phrasing, likened by Terry to Lenderman, Steve Earle, Drive-By Truckers and Being There-era Wilco. A concept record about highway wandering, bar to bar.
lineage: Draws on outlaw country and Wilco's Being There as touchstones; part of the same wave of young Southern indie-twang songwriters as Thomas Dollbaum and i26connector.
borderline_note: Real Bandcamp handle is oldst4r (band tags itself 'oldstar'); a different band uses the plain 'oldstar' handle.

label: Self-released
description: Zachary James's efficient, hooky home-recording project: 90s alt-rock and Pavement/Big Star-style jangle folded into twangy, deceptively simple songs; Terry's most-played album of 2023, later reissued by Double Double Whammy.
lineage: Part of the same Burlington scene as Greg Freeman and Florry, drawing on Judee Sill, Alex Chilton and Elliott Smith-style idiosyncratic songwriting.

album: I Saw A Galloping Horse Cover No Ground
label: Anything Bagel
description: Joseph Barresi's third Chico States LP, self-tagged 'ANTI-AMERICANA': dusky, encyclopedic Americana with pedal steel and scrappy harmonies, mixing personal minutiae with train-line and travel history.
lineage: Works in the same 'cosmic Americana' vein Terry links to Lomax-style folk documentation, adjacent to the Northeast's alt-country underground.

label: Self-released
description: A.S. Wilson's second Convinced Friend LP, tracked live in a day with Bradford Krieger: eight compact, forceful tracks fusing serene twang with apocalyptic indie rock, reflecting on his native Houma, Louisiana as its coastline erodes.
lineage: Produced by Bradford Krieger (Horse Jumper of Love, Friendship), tying Convinced Friend into the Northeast slowcore/twang production network.

album: How to Get Away with Nothing
label: Candlepin Records
description: Columbus songwriter Abel's self-lacerating, ramshackle country-jangle LP, co-released by Julia's War, Candlepin and Pleasure Tapes; loud guitar music for quiet people, per Terry.
lineage: Part of the small-label DIY twang network (Julia's War, Candlepin) alongside Ohio- and Midwest-based indie-country peers like Spencer Radcliffe.

label: Self-released
description: New Orleans band's 13-song LP steeped in Gulf Coast heat and road-worn twang; loose, rowdy cowpunk energy carried across tracks like the title cut and 'Swamp'.
lineage: Part of the current New Orleans indie-twang scene alongside Thomas Dollbaum, touring with Kurt Vile.

label: Self-released
description: Owen Burton's debut as Ovven, a fuzz-guitar alt-country tour-de-force produced by Alex Farrar (MJ Lenderman, Wednesday, Indigo De Souza), praised by SiriusXM Outlaw Country as an instant classic.
lineage: Shares a producer with Wednesday and MJ Lenderman, plugging Ovven directly into the Drop of Sun/Alex Farrar wing of the Asheville-adjacent indie-twang network.

album: Watch Me Drive Them Dogs Wild
label: Self-released
description: Pittsburgh songwriter's breakout LP: warbling steel and outlaw-tinged guitars swelling into feedback-heavy catharsis, produced by Colin Miller and Alex Farrar at Drop of Sun; songs of loss, land and family community.
lineage: Ties Merce Lemon into the Asheville production network (Colin Miller, Alex Farrar, Xandy Chelmis of Wednesday on pedal steel) shared with Florry and Wednesday.

label: Fire Talk
description: Wild Pink's sixth LP, the band's most twang-coded record: driving, intense indie rock with Xandy Chelmis of Wednesday on pedal steel, framing searing, funny, wrenching lyrics about contemporary malaise.
lineage: Marks Wild Pink's turn toward the Core indie-twang sound via Chelmis's pedal steel; ruled into C1 as a specific stylistic pivot rather than the band's whole catalogue.
key_tracks: Round Of Applause At The End Of The World
borderline_note: Wild Pink's earlier albums (Wild Pink, Yolk in the Fur, A Billion Little Lights, ILYSM, Dulling the Horns) are straighter indie rock and are NOT included here; only Still Coming Down was ruled into C1.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Austin quartet's debut: blue-collar, plainspoken indie rock with Replacements swagger and War on Drugs-style desert-rock riffs from guitarist Jake Ames, writing about home and growing up around conservatives.
lineage: Bandleader Tyler Jordan met Jake Ames at Kerrville Folk Festival song swaps (where they also crossed paths with Buck Meek and Adrianne Lenker); Keeled Scales labelmates of Katy Kirby.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Good Looks' second LP, written after guitarist Jake Ames survived a serious traffic accident: conversational, big-hearted indie rock with big riffs, framed by the band as a document of resilience.
lineage: Continues the band's blue-collar Austin storytelling from Bummer Year into a bigger, more electric sound.

label: Fire Talk
description: Blair Howerton's second Why Bonnie LP: twangy, expansive rock that widens the country-coded debut 90 in November into more cinematic, ambitious soundscapes, with fiddle and harmonies still anchoring the quieter moments.
lineage: Follows 90 in November's Waxahatchee/Wednesday-adjacent country sound before opening out toward Broken Social Scene/HAIM-style pop-rock.

label: Third Man Records
description: Nance's Third Man Records debut with his full band Mowed Sound: interlocking, jammed-out guitar rock in a direct Crazy Horse lineage, called some of his best work yet.
lineage: A Midwest continuation of the Crazy Horse guitar-jam trunk line that also runs through Wednesday and MJ Lenderman.

album: May You Live Forever in Cowboy Heaven
label: Self-released
description: Nashville band's ramshackle, woozy-twang record with fiddle and Built to Spill/Elephant 6-style energy; lyrics name-check Big Thief, Neil Young, the Replacements and Silver Jews.
lineage: Explicitly draws on Neil Young and Silver Jews, situating Dialup Ghost within the same trunk lines as the rest of the Core.
